calls.title: CFI & GrowthBook Demo
calls.summary: The team plans to complete the platform evaluation by mid-July, with a decision expected by the end of July, led by CTO Martin Kiuru. The evaluation approach emphasizes integration with existing tools like GitHub and GitLab, addressing the need for tracking feature impact and justifying development costs. The business objectives include establishing a data-driven management framework to align feature development with metrics such as net profit and customer engagement, particularly through AI-driven features. GrowthBook's architecture supports self-hosted deployments, integrating seamlessly with Databricks and offering extensive feature management capabilities. With a pricing model based on seat licenses, next steps involve a follow-up meeting for further collaboration between teams.
calls.keywords: feature flagging, experimentation, data-driven product management, GrowthBook, engineering integration, databricks

calls.title: CFI + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team is in an early evaluation phase for selecting an experimentation platform, prioritizing engineering readiness and feature toggling support before making a decision. Currently, they lack feature toggling, which is essential for maximizing Growthbook's capabilities. The timeline for selection has shifted to Q4 or early Q1. Martin Kiuru highlighted the need for a unified dashboard to manage deployments, experiments, and results, while James Shannon proposed parallel engagement to align Growthbook integration with engineering changes. Metrics are crucial, with KPIs based on customer lifetime value and other features, while successful technical integration with existing workflows remains a priority. The next check-in is planned for mid-September.
calls.keywords: Feature toggles, experimentation platform, GrowthBook, metrics tracking, A/B testing, AI integration

calls.title: CFI & GrowthBook Catch Up
calls.summary:
# CFI & GrowthBook Catch Up
Date: 2026-09-16 | Duration: 29.25m

## Summary
The discussion covered GrowthBook’s planned Q1 feature-toggling pilot, which will test tracking and rollout methods and support future dashboards and product analytics. GrowthBook also presented a natural-language AI assistant for creating feature flags, CLI access for technical users, and funnel metrics for tracking multi-step experiment journeys and identifying bottlenecks. Version 5.1, including AI enhancements, is expected in a few weeks. Pricing was described as an approximately $30,000 annual base license plus $1,000 per seat beyond 25 seats, with enterprise features and support included. A 30-day proof of concept provides full feature and support access, subject to agreement on pricing and privacy terms, and can transition into an annual contract. GrowthBook stores login credentials and targeting attributes in its control plane while customer data remains in the customer’s warehouse. Support includes solutions engineering, training, and project-based organizational segmentation. The customer plans to revisit the evaluation in mid-November and may trial two to three platforms.

## Keywords
feature toggling, AI assistant, funnel metrics, enterprise pricing, proof of concept, data privacy

## Action Items

**Martin Kiuru**
Reconnect mid-November to discuss progress on feature toggling adoption and pilot phase (25:50)

**George Lakas**
Update internal Excel sheet with new GrowthBook feature details (21:15)

**James Shannon**
Send updated transcript and details of new GrowthBook features including AI assistant and funnel metrics (21:15)
Provide a summary email about upcoming GrowthBook 5.1 release with new features (15:26)
Schedule a follow-up placeholder meeting for end of November to continue discussions and trial planning (26:45)
Continue to provide occasional feature updates relevant to CFI without overwhelming with communications (27:10)
Introduce solutions engineer to support the proof of concept implementation when initiated (17:50)
